storyNotes.originalText: Pharaoh's wine taster and baker were thrown in prison. Both had special DREAMS from God.
storyNotes.cleanText: Pharaoh's wine taster and baker were thrown in prison. Both had special dreams from God.

storyNotes.originalText: In the wine taster's dream, he squeezed GRAPES from a vine into Pharaoh's cup.
storyNotes.cleanText: In the wine taster's dream, he squeezed grapes from a vine into Pharaoh's cup.

storyNotes.originalText: Joseph explained, "In three days, Pharaoh will give you back your old JOB."
storyNotes.cleanText: Joseph explained, "In three days, Pharaoh will give you back your old job."

storyNotes.originalText: Joseph said, "Speak to PHARAOH about my story. Ask him to get me out of this prison."
storyNotes.cleanText: Joseph said, "Speak to pharaoh about my story. Ask him to get me out of this prison."

storyNotes.originalText: In the baker's dream, BIRDS picked at the bread baskets he carried on his head.
storyNotes.cleanText: In the baker's dream, birds picked at the bread baskets he carried on his head.

storyNotes.originalText: Joseph explained, "In three days, Pharaoh will have you KILLED."
storyNotes.cleanText: Joseph explained, "In three days, Pharaoh will have you killed."

storyNotes.originalText: Everything happened just as Joseph said, but the wine taster FORGOT about Joseph.
storyNotes.cleanText: Everything happened just as Joseph said, but the wine taster forgot about Joseph.

facts.statement: Pharaoh’s wine taster and baker joined Joseph in prison.
The wine taster and baker were thrown into a bottomless pit.
Both men had dreams that Joseph helped them understand.
The wine taster dreamed about baskets of eggs on his head.
The wine taster dreamed about a vine with three branches.
The vine in the wine taster’s dream had seven branches.
Joseph said the wine taster would get his job back in three days.
Joseph told the baker he would get his job back in three days.
Birds ate bread from baskets in the baker’s dream.
In the baker’s dream, cows ate the bread from his baskets.
Joseph asked the wine taster to tell Pharaoh about him.
The wine taster told Pharaoh about Joseph as soon as he left prison.
Pharaoh had the baker killed three days later.
The wine taster got his job back but forgot Joseph.

circleMistakes.paragraph: Pharaoh's wine taster and bodyguard were thrown into prison with Joseph. The wine taster dreamed of a banana vine with three branches. He squeezed grapes into a basket for Pharaoh. Joseph explained that the wine taster would get his job back in three years. The baker dreamed of birds eating fish from baskets on his head. When the wine taster went free, he remembered Joseph right away.

finishStory.markedParagraph: Pharaoh's [wine] taster and [baker] went sent to [prison]. They were there with Joseph. Both of them had [dreams] that troubled them. The wine taster dreamed about squeezing [grapes] into Pharaoh's cup. The baker dreamed of birds eating [bread] from baskets on his [head]. The two men explained their dreams to Joseph. Because of God's [help], Joseph explained the [meaning] of these dreams. Three days later, Pharaoh punished the baker, but gave the wine taster his [job] back, just like Joseph said. After [leaving] prison, the wine taster [forgot] Joseph.

reviewFlags.text: Source memory verse is an ESV excerpt of Psalm 23:4a. Prepared activities use a BSB excerpt ending “for You are with me;” Verify the exact passage boundary, punctuation, child readability and intended publication permissions.
Review the six Multiple Choice questions and their twelve suggested wrong answers for age suitability and clarity.
Review the six newly composed false facts and the three non-overlapping True/False-related module selections.

The original lesson describes the baker being killed and the later fate of his body. Preserve the original Story Note and questions; check whether the child-facing activities use the right level of detail.
Check that Odd Words and Checkboxes are truly distinct and that suggested distractors are clearly not part of the current story.
Review six deliberate errors and the correction key. They should be clear, not too hard or repetitive.
Do not suggest Joseph was freed in Genesis 40; the wine taster returned to his work, the baker was killed, and Joseph remained in prison and was forgotten.
Before approving, test every live generator, the official preflight and all three numbered worksheet presets. Draft content has not been tested in the app.
All seven Story Notes are preserved exactly, with the original emphasized words, and all teaching/review questions are separately retained.
Review harder lesson words such as Pharaoh, wine taster, prison and the memory verse’s “shadow of death” for the intended ages.
